newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark vol off boil, puts still popular.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark vol off boil, puts still popular.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options traded on LIFFE is likely to reconsider the recent rally, and start to slide back down, traders said on Thursday.
Over recent weeks speculation that there would be a change in the German repo rate drove Euromark volatility higher, shaking it out of the torpor which had reigned since the beginning of the year.
Although investors are still buying protection in the form of puts, the swell of activity seen earlier in the week has slowed, particularly from U.S. houses.
"Volatility is looking very expensive," said a trader at U.S. house in London. "Everything seems to have gone quiet on the rate front for the time being."

September volatility was trading at 12.07/13.8 percent, unchanged from the prior close, while December was off about 0.10 at 15.3/16.2 percent. March 1998 options were up at around 19.0 percent mid, compared with 17.5 percent on Wednesday.
September Euromark futures were unchanged at 96.70, while December was up 0.02 at 96.56 by 1130 GMT. March futures were up 0.01 at 96.44.
A salesman at a European bank in London said put buying was still the predominant trade.
"We don't think the Bundesbank will do anything short- to medium-term," he said. "People who are long puts will die off and then vol will follow."
He said he advised looking to convergence trades at the short end of the European options market.
"Look to sell puts in March Eurolira, where vol is going to be quite stable, and buy the mark puts when the vol has a 14 percent handle," he said.
March Eurolira options were trading at a volatility of 16.65/17.0 percent, compared with 17.11 percent previously.
The 96.50 strike September Eurolira puts were active, with more than 2,500 lots traded. In the December series, 1,000 puts at 96.00 went through.
